metadata.title: Hypervelocity runaways from the Large Magellanic Cloud

evidence.quote: the one HVS in the southern hemisphere, HE 0437-5439
the one HVS in the southern hemisphere, HE 0437-5439, which was discovered by Edelmann et al. (2005)
the 6D kinematics of the known HVSs are consistent with the expectations for an LMC origin
in addition to HE 0437-5439 (Edelmann et al. 2005) and US 708 (Hirsch et al. 2005), with recent updated proper motions from the Hubble Space Telescope (Brown et al. 2015)
which has previously been used to explain the helium-rich HVS US708 (Justham et al. 2009; Geier et al. 2013)

notes: HE 0437-5439: follow_up; T:p6-b8 calls it the one HVS in the southern hemisphere and says it was discovered by Edelmann et al., while T:p8-b2 includes it among the known HVSs whose 6D kinematics are tested against an LMC origin. US 708 (also printed US708): follow_up; T:p8-b2 lists it among known HVSs and T:p8-b5 calls it a helium-rich HVS. I treated the paper's HVS terminology as Galactic unbound per T:p1-b11. The unnamed known B-type HVS population is not separately listed because no individual identifiers are supplied. Sk-67 2 is not included: T:p9-b1 calls it a 'candidate hypervelocity star' in the Lennon et al. LMC-runaway context and bases this on a peculiar velocity, but the paper does not establish Galactic unboundedness. R 71 and Sk-71 42 (T:p9-b1) are LMC velocity outliers not claimed Galactic unbound; CD14-A08 (T:p8-b5) is a possible LMC/MW-origin subdwarf, and J004330.06+405258.4 (T:p9-b2) is described as likely unbound from M31 rather than the Milky Way.

HE 0437-5439: HE 0437-5439 is identified only as one of the known B-type hypervelocity stars. The paper mentions it qualitatively (T:p6-b8): an LMC origin had previously been explored for it, its flight time exceeds the main-sequence lifetime, and possible ejection mechanisms are a massive black hole or dynamical ejection from a cluster. It is also included among the known HVSs plotted in Figure 3, but no individual numerical values (coordinates, distance, proper motion, radial velocity, space velocity, Galactocentric radius, or bound probability) are reported for this star in the text or tables, and it cannot be separated from other unlabeled plotted points. Therefore no quantities meeting the extraction rules are available.

US 708: The paper mentions US 708 only qualitatively. At T:p8-b2 it includes US 708 among known HVSs with recent updated HST proper motions from Brown et al. (2015), but reports no numerical position, distance, proper motion, radial velocity, or other target-specific quantities. At T:p8-b5 it again mentions US 708 as a helium-rich HVS in the context of CD14-A08, also without numerical values. Figure 3 shows known HVSs collectively but provides no star-by-star labels or tabulated values for US 708, so no quantities can be extracted without adding unsupported information.
